findings.title: The shared control-artifact validator accepts repeated separators as a noncanonical stored path
findings.reproduction: At c16a36424fb97cb95347261ebab248f128b5d931, call taskctl.canonical_control_artifact_path with `planning/governance-recovery-approvals//GRR-0001.B00.remediation-01.evidence.json` and prefix `planning/governance-recovery-approvals`. It succeeds and returns the raw double-slash spelling while resolving to the canonical file. The same behavior applies to `artifacts/evidence//W1.A03.B00.json` when used by the appended-amendment evidence entry. tools/taskctl.py constructs PurePosixPath before checking parts; PurePosixPath collapses the empty segment, so the intended empty-segment rejection is ineffective. Existing R02 tests cover absolute, backslash, dot, dot-dot, symlink, and junction forms but omit repeated separators.
findings.requiredRemediation: Reject repeated separators and every other spelling whose raw value differs from its canonical PurePosix form before resolution or access. Add command-entry tests for recovery evidence, review ledgers, and appended-amendment evidence using internal double separators, and prove no noncanonical spelling is stored or read.
